title: Ragnarök: the end of the Nordic world
subtitle: Norse mythology
subject: mythologie
description: Not a divine punishment, but an accepted fate: the gods of Asgard fall, the world burns, then is reborn greener. The Nordic apocalypse.

hero.hook: The gods know they are going to die. They go there anyway. Then, under the ashes, the earth turns green again.

blocks.text: The **Ragnarök** is the end of the world in Norse mythology. It is often translated as “twilight of the gods”, but the exact meaning is rather “destiny of the powers”. It is not a punishment falling from the sky, nor a definitive nothingness.
It is an inevitable **ZZ** tragedy: the order of **Asgard** collapses in a final battle against chaos. And yet, this chaos prepares a rebirth. The end is just one stage of the cycle.
The expression "twilight of the gods" comes from a confusion between the Old Norse words "rök" (fate) and "rökr" (twilight), popularized by Wagner.

It all starts with the **Fimbulwinter**: a Great Winter of three years without summer. The cold breaks families apart. Violence is becoming widespread. Then the magic locks give way. The wolf **Fenrir** breaks his chains. Its mouth touches heaven and earth.

blocks.caption: Fenrir chained: the day he frees himself, the world turns upside down.

blocks.text: The serpent **Jörmungandr**, which encircles the continents, struggles in the ocean: tidal waves and poisons. Cosmic wolves devour the Sun and the Moon. **Loki**, escaped, commands the , a ship made of nails of the dead, loaded with giants towards the last battlefield. [[Naglfar]]

sections.title: The plain where the gods fall

blocks.text: The confrontation takes place on the plain of **Vígríðr**. , the watchman of the gods, sounds his horn. The gods of Asgard go there knowing they will lose. Everyone faces their enemy. [[Heimdall]]

blocks.caption: Ragnarök: gods, monsters and fire on the same plain.

blocks.text: **Odin**, father of the gods, is devoured by Fenrir. His son Víðarr avenges his father. **Thor** crushes Jörmungandr with , but dies from its venom after nine steps. Then **Surtr**, a fiery giant from , sets the nine worlds ablaze. The earth is sinking beneath the ocean. [[Mjölnir]] [[Muspellheim]]
The god Freyr dies without his magic sword: he had offered it out of love to obtain the hand of the giantess Gerd. Even love has a price, in these myths.

sections.title: After the fire, the earth turns green again

blocks.text: What distinguishes Ragnarök from linear apocalypses is the return. Once the flames are extinguished, the earth emerges from the waves, greener and more fertile. The fields give without being sown.

blocks.caption: Yggdrasil, the world tree: shelter for survivors and promise of continuation.

blocks.text: A new generation of gods survives: **Baldr** returns from the dead; Thor's sons, Magni and Móði, inherit the hammer. Two humans, **Líf** and **Lífþrasir**, hid in  and fed on dew. Their names mean “Life” and “Full of life”. Humanity begins again. [[Yggdrasil]]

In the 19th century, **Richard Wagner** popularized his , the “Twilight of the Gods”: the end of an order based on broken oaths. For the Ancient Scandinavians, the message was simpler and harder: if the end is certain, there remains the choice of courage. [[Götterdämmerung]]

brings this story closer to other ends of the world: long winter, celestial combat, flood, rebirth. As winter precedes spring, Ragnarök is not just a death. It's a metamorphosis. [[Comparative apocalypticism]]

The **Ragnarök** is not nothingness: it is the accepted destiny of the gods, a battle where Asgard falls, followed by an earth that is reborn. The Nordic lesson: act with courage, even without hope of victory.
